reference.source: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology / Stiehm's Immune Deficiencies
clinicalPearls: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in ADA2 (formerly CECR1), presenting as a monogenic vasculitis often resembling polyarteritis nodosa
Early-onset recurrent ischaemic and haemorrhagic strokes, frequently lacunar and affecting the deep brain, are a defining and devastating feature
Livedo racemosa, systemic inflammation, fevers and features overlapping with polyarteritis nodosa are common
The phenotype is broad and can include immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinaemia, cytopenias and bone marrow failure, and lymphoproliferation
Diagnosis is supported by markedly low or absent plasma ADA2 enzyme activity, confirmed by ADA2 genetic testing
Anti-tumour-necrosis-factor therapy is effective at preventing strokes and controlling vasculitis and is preferred over antiplatelet or anticoagulant strategies, which risk haemorrhage
Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation can correct the haematological and immune phenotype in severe cases
reference.pathophysiology: DADA2 is caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the ADA2 gene, which encodes the secreted enzyme adenosine deaminase 2. Unlike the intracellular ADA1 enzyme whose deficiency causes severe combined immunodeficiency, ADA2 is released chiefly by cells of the myeloid lineage and acts as a growth factor influencing endothelial integrity and the differentiation of monocytes and macrophages. Loss of ADA2 skews macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, impairs endothelial stability, and produces a vasculopathy affecting small and medium vessels, together with excess tumour necrosis factor-driven inflammation. The endothelial and vascular damage underlies the strokes and vasculitis, while effects on haematopoiesis and lymphocytes account for the immunodeficiency and cytopenias.
additionalDifferentials: Antiphospholipid syndrome and other thrombophilic causes of young stroke
Common variable immunodeficiency (for the immunodeficiency phenotype)
Other type I interferonopathies and monogenic autoinflammatory vasculopathies
additionalInvestigations: Neuroimaging (MRI with vascular imaging) for lacunar infarcts and haemorrhage
Full blood count and bone marrow evaluation where cytopenias are present
Acute phase reactants and vasculitis workup
redFlags: Acute stroke or new focal neurological deficit in a child or young adult
Intracranial haemorrhage, particularly if antithrombotic therapy is being considered
Progressive cytopenias or bone marrow failure
Severe systemic vasculitis with organ ischaemia
reference.prognosis: Untreated DADA2 carries a high burden of recurrent stroke and cumulative neurological disability, but tumour-necrosis-factor inhibition markedly reduces stroke recurrence and controls vasculitis; severe haematological or immune disease may require transplantation, and early diagnosis substantially improves outcome.
pitfalls: Treating recurrent strokes with antiplatelet or anticoagulant agents, which increase the risk of catastrophic haemorrhage in DADA2
Diagnosing idiopathic polyarteritis nodosa in a young patient without testing ADA2
Overlooking the immunodeficiency and cytopenia phenotype that can present without prominent vasculitis
Delaying tumour necrosis factor inhibition, which is the key stroke-preventing therapy
management: Establish tumour necrosis factor inhibition (anti-TNF biologic therapy) as the mainstay to prevent recurrent strokes and suppress the vasculitis
Do not use antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy for stroke prevention, given the haemorrhage risk; control disease with TNF blockade
Use corticosteroids to control acute inflammatory flares while biologic therapy is established
Manage immunodeficiency with immunoglobulin replacement and prompt treatment of infections
Treat cytopenias and bone marrow failure with haematology input, escalating to haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, which can be curative for severe haematological or immune disease
Monitor with MRI and vascular imaging of the brain, full blood count and acute-phase reactants for strokes and disease activity
Provide genetic counselling and family testing for this autosomal recessive ADA2 disorder, pursuing early diagnosis to improve outcomes
